name: State of California
policy_note: Structural research pointer only. NO substantive statutory rules — student packets are facts-only; finding the controlling law is the exercise. Code-level locators are navigational aids. Instructor notes may cite specifics, verified at publish.

trial_court.name: Superior Court of California
trial_court.note: The single trial court of general jurisdiction, organized by county (e.g., 'Superior Court of California, County of ___'). Operates specialized divisions for juvenile and family matters.

specialty_divisions.juvenile: Juvenile Division of the Superior Court — delinquency proceedings under Welfare & Institutions Code (petitions typically brought under WIC § 602). Records confidential; minors identified by initials.
specialty_divisions.family: Family Law Division of the Superior Court — dissolution, custody, support, and community-property division.

intermediate_appellate.name: California Court of Appeal
intermediate_appellate.note: Intermediate appellate court, organized into six Appellate Districts.

shape_specific_notes.juvenile: California juvenile delinquency proceedings run under the Welfare & Institutions Code (WIC), not the adult Penal Code process; dispositions, wardship, and sealing follow WIC. Cases captioned 'In re <initials>, a Minor.' Students research current WIC procedure themselves.
shape_specific_notes.dissolution: California is a COMMUNITY-PROPERTY state — property and debt acquired during marriage are presumptively community property divided equally at dissolution; this is the deliberate contrast the m19 shape teaches. Dissolution captioned 'In re the Marriage of <A> and <B>.' Students research the current Family Code framework themselves.
shape_specific_notes.noncompete_crossref: California broadly voids employee non-compete covenants by statute — the contrast point referenced by the m16 (NY) shape.

cases.reporters: Cal. Rptr. 3d and P.3d; official Cal.5th / Cal. App. 5th

navigational_code_areas: Juvenile delinquency: Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code, Part 1, Chapter 2 (Juvenile Court Law) — a starting point for m18.
Dissolution and community property: Cal. Fam. Code (Divisions 6 and 7) — a starting point for m19.

disclaimer: Structural/navigational reference only, current as of 2026. Verify all law against the official sources above; nothing here is legal advice.
